## Which tour includes Topoxté?

Our selection features **{{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}** with a scheduled visit to [Topoxté](/guatemala/place/topoxte/). This archaeological site lies on an island in Lake Yaxhá in northern [Guatemala](/guatemala/). It is especially appealing to travelers who want to explore several ancient Maya centers, seeing both vast urban complexes and smaller island settlements surrounded by water and forest.

On the [Guatemala, Honduras and Belize itinerary](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-honduras-belize/), **day 7** is titled "Flores — Yaxhá and Topoxté." The program explicitly includes both sites and a return to the Bolontiku hotel after the excursion. **Day 8** is devoted separately to Tikal. Topoxté is therefore part of a substantial archaeological segment in Petén, not merely an optional suggestion on a list of possible visits.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_gvatemala_gonduras_i_beliz}}

We update this selection when itineraries change. When choosing a trip, read the actual archaeological day: a visit to [Yaxhá](/guatemala/place/yaxha/) or [Tikal and Flores](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/) does not in itself confirm a stop on the island. The [general Guatemala tours catalog](/guatemala/tour/) includes trips with other combinations of sites.

## Topoxté and Yaxhá: two different archaeological centers

[Yaxhá](/guatemala/place/yaxha/) is a Maya city on the lagoon's shore, with temples, squares, acropolises and ancient roads. [Topoxté](/guatemala/place/topoxte/) occupies an island in the same body of water. Ceremonial and public buildings survive among the trees; reaching the island requires a boat crossing.

Their historical importance differs too. Yaxhá was a major urban center of Classic Maya civilization. Research into Topoxté is especially important for the **Postclassic period**: settlements on islands in the lagoon continued to exist in later eras, after the importance of many earlier urban centers had changed. Exploring both sites in sequence reveals more of the variety of Maya settlements than visiting a single famous temple.

The surrounding Yaxhá–Nakum–Naranjo National Park protects archaeological sites, tropical forests and wetland landscapes. Birds and other animals live here, although sightings depend on chance. For a broader exploration of Guatemala's natural environment, compare [wildlife and nature itineraries](/interests/wildlife/tours/guatemala/); for ancient civilizations, see [cultural and historical journeys](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/guatemala/). Whether any specific trip includes Topoxté must be checked separately.

## How the route reaches the island and continues afterward

On the current tour, several regions of Central America are visited before the island. The itinerary first takes in [Antigua](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/), [Chichicastenango](/guatemala/place/chichicastenango/) and [Lake Atitlán](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/). The group then visits [Copán](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/) in Honduras and returns to Guatemala via [Quiriguá](/guatemala/place/quirigua/) and [Río Dulce](/guatemala/place/rio-dulce/).

After arrival in the northern region, two archaeological days follow:

| Day | Main sights |
|---|---|
| 7 | [Yaxhá](/guatemala/place/yaxha/) and Topoxté Island |
| 8 | [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/) |

On day 7, travelers return to the hotel after visiting the two complexes. On day 8, they explore Tikal, where tall temples of the ancient city rise above the forest canopy. The route then continues into [Belize](/belize/), rounding off its archaeological segment by the Caribbean coast.

This sequence suits travelers who want to trace Maya history across several sites. It also takes time: with a short vacation, it is sensible to identify your highest-priority site before choosing a longer international itinerary.

## How Topoxté, Yaxhá, Tikal and Copán differ

Each destination serves a different purpose in the journey. It is easier to consider these differences before booking a tour.

| Site | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| [Topoxté](/guatemala/place/topoxte/) | Maya island settlement |
| [Yaxhá](/guatemala/place/yaxha/) | Ancient city, lagoon and forest |
| [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/) | Monumental temples |
| [Copán](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/) | Stelae and stone carving |
| [Quiriguá](/guatemala/place/quirigua/) | Carved Maya monuments |

**Topoxté** adds island archaeology to the larger cities. **Yaxhá** lets you discover the layout of an ancient center along forest paths. **Tikal** conveys the size of a major Classic-period city. **Copán** is especially prized for its stone sculptures and inscriptions, while Quiriguá is associated with monumental stelae.

On the [tour via Topoxté](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-honduras-belize/), these experiences form one extended sequence. For a trip focused on northern Guatemala, also explore [tours via Yaxhá](/guatemala/place/yaxha/tour/) or [journeys through Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/tour/): the sites and countries visited may differ.

## What to know before visiting the island

Topoxté lies on an island, so boat transport is necessary. Guatemala's official cultural information system mentions boat services via the park's visitor center. However, **the availability of a boat does not guarantee its inclusion in the price of a particular tour**. Transfers, tickets, guiding and the order of visits depend on the selected itinerary.

Bring closed, non-slip footwear, water, a hat and rain protection. Damp paths and boarding a boat can be challenging for travelers with limited mobility. If that matters to you, assess the island segment specifically, including walking distances between structures.

For a day trip from Flores, allow time for the drive to the archaeological park, exploring Yaxhá, the boat crossing and the return journey. Seeing two sites takes longer than visiting just one. Admission rules, trail conditions and the possibility of crossing to the island should be checked for your travel date, as arrangements within a protected area can change.

## Questions about tours via Topoxté

### Are Topoxté and Yaxhá the same place?

No. [Yaxhá](/guatemala/place/yaxha/) is on the lagoon shore, while [Topoxté](/guatemala/place/topoxte/) is a separate archaeological site on an island. Ada Tours' current itinerary visits both on the same day.

### Does every tour through Petén include Topoxté?

No. [Petén](/guatemala/place/peten/) has numerous archaeological sites and natural areas. A tour may include Tikal or Yaxhá without visiting the island. This page selects itineraries with Topoxté as part of the main route.

### Is Tikal visited on the same day?

On the current [Guatemala, Honduras and Belize tour](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-honduras-belize/), Yaxhá and Topoxté are scheduled for day 7 and Tikal for day 8. They are separate excursion days.

### Is a boat required?

Yes. Topoxté is on an island in Yaxhá Lagoon. Check the itinerary for the precise crossing arrangements and services paid for.

### Who will enjoy a tour via Topoxté?

Travelers who want to compare several Maya cities and settlements in Guatemala and Honduras before continuing to Belize. For a trip to a single archaeological complex, it is more practical to compare shorter programs via [Yaxhá](/guatemala/place/yaxha/tour/) and [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/tour/).

## Yaxhá: an ancient Maya city between forest and lagoons

**Yaxhá stands out for its combination of archaeology and natural surroundings.** The ruins are in Yaxhá–Nakum–Naranjo National Park, amid Petén's tropical forest. Unlike a museum with individual exhibits, you explore the ancient city plan on foot, walking from one square to another along stone roads and seeing how the buildings relate to the surrounding landscape.

Yaxhá was one of the region's political and ceremonial centers. Pyramid temples, acropolises, ball courts and other structures survive within the complex. A visit offers a glimpse of a city that developed in relation to neighboring centers of the ancient Maya civilization.

### What to see along the archaeological route

Begin with the main ceremonial squares and sections of the former city roads. These are good places to examine the positions of temples and the connections between different quarters. The walk can then continue to viewpoints above the treetops, where access is permitted.

One of Yaxhá's most recognizable sights is its forest-fringed lagoons. From certain elevated spots, the water is visible beyond the dense greenery. Late-day visits depend on park hours, access to the structures and the return transfer: a sunset photograph in a guidebook does not mean every pyramid can be visited after closing time.

Birds and other tropical forest animals can be heard along the paths. Treat this as an opportunity to observe the ecosystem rather than a promise of seeing any particular species. A relaxed pace and attention to the trails make both archaeological exploration and nature watching more enjoyable.

## How Yaxhá differs from Tikal

[Tikal and Flores](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/) often anchor a first visit to Petén: they offer a famous archaeological complex and a convenient base for arranging excursions. Yaxhá reveals another part of Maya historical geography, where the ruins are closely associated with the Yaxhá and Sacnab lagoons.

| Place | Main focus |
|---|---|
| Yaxhá | Lagoons and forest beside the temples |
| Tikal | A large temple complex |
| Flores | A base for exploring Petén |

Your best choice depends on the time available. On a short trip, it is better to explore one complex thoroughly than rush through two. With an extra day, you can add Yaxhá and compare the layouts and natural settings of different Maya cities.

The park system also includes Nakum and Naranjo. However, the presence of these names in the protected area's title does not mean all three ancient cities are covered by an ordinary excursion: distances, roads and visiting arrangements differ.

## How to organize a trip to Yaxhá

Yaxhá lies in the [Petén region](/guatemala/place/peten/) of northern Guatemala. Visits are often arranged from the Flores area, combining historical exploration with opportunities to observe nature. Allow time for transport in both directions, walking around the site, stops at monuments and a margin for weather.

The tropical climate affects comfort: days can be hot and humid, while stones and earth become slippery after rain. Bring water, sun and insect protection, comfortable closed shoes and lightweight rainwear. Check the current visiting rules, especially possible restrictions on climbing structures.

### Yaxhá on a Guatemala–Belize itinerary

Northern Guatemala can be combined with Belize's archaeological sites on one journey if both countries are actually included in the tour. But proximity on the map does not remove border formalities, road delays or dependence on the chosen crossing point. On a multi-country trip, establish the actual sequence and travel time before adding extra sites.

[Tours featuring Guatemala](/guatemala/tour/) vary in whether they visit Petén and how much archaeology they include. If Yaxhá is your particular interest, verify that it appears in the day-by-day itinerary and list of places: mentioning Petén or Tikal is not the same as arranging a separate visit to Yaxhá.

## Frequently asked questions about Yaxhá

### Is Yaxhá the same place as Tikal?

No. It is a distinct ancient Maya city. [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/) and Yaxhá are in the same larger region but differ in their archaeological complexes and natural settings.

### Can you see the lagoon during a visit to Yaxhá?

Yes. The Yaxhá and Sacnab lagoons are important features of the landscape. The view from a particular vantage point depends on the approved route, visibility and access conditions.

### Should I set aside a separate day for Yaxhá?

For a relaxed visit with travel from the Flores area, plan a separate outing. If time is limited, compare Yaxhá with other sites in [Petén](/guatemala/place/peten/) and choose a priority rather than an exhausting series of transfers.

## Yaxhá as an optional excursion: when to add it

[Yaxhá](/guatemala/place/yaxha/) is an ancient Maya city amid the tropical forests and lagoons of northern Guatemala. Unlike [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/), which is an obligatory standalone day on several tours, Yaxhá can be an additional option if enough time remains after arriving in [Petén](/guatemala/place/peten/).

On the [12-day Guatemala and Belize — Into the World of the Maya tour](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-belize-maya-world-12-days/), day 6 includes a transfer from Antigua to Guatemala City airport, a domestic flight to Petén, a meeting on arrival and hotel check-in. After that, travelers can rest at the hotel, take a walk around [Flores](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/) or book an [excursion to Yaxhá](/guatemala/yaxha/yaxha-optional-visit/). It **costs extra**; timing, transport, guiding and the specific price are agreed when booking.

This differs from the [catalog of tours with Yaxhá included](/guatemala/place/yaxha/tour/), where the archaeological site is already part of the main route. If visiting Yaxhá must be guaranteed regardless of flight timing, start by comparing those included-itinerary options.

## Where Yaxhá fits among the main journey stages

The key part of the 12-day itinerary looks like this:

| Day | Main event |
|---|---|
| 6 | Flight to Petén |
| 7 | Guided visit to [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/) |
| 8 | Travel towards [Belize](/belize/) |

It is the free part of **day 6** that offers a possible Yaxhá visit. The next day's main itinerary includes guided sightseeing at Tikal and lunch within the complex, followed by time to relax by Lake Petén Itzá. The following morning begins with an overland border crossing into Belize towards [San Ignacio](/belize/place/san-ignacio/).

The feasibility of adding Yaxhá therefore depends on the actual flight arrival time and road journey to the archaeological park. Do not assume the whole of day 6 is free: it already involves a flight and transfers. The return trip to the hotel, meals, visiting hours and the need for rest before the next morning should all be planned together.

## What Yaxhá adds when Tikal is already scheduled

Yaxhá and Tikal both illuminate Maya civilization, but their archaeological landscapes are different. [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/) is famous for large temple complexes, while [Yaxhá](/guatemala/place/yaxha/) stands among forests and the Yaxhá and Sacnab lagoons. Squares, temples, ancient roads and acropolises survive in the archaeological park. Its wooded setting makes the walk an encounter with both history and nature.

Yaxhá–Nakum–Naranjo National Park is in the Petén department. It protects the archaeological remains of several Maya cities and their surrounding ecosystems. A visit to Yaxhá makes it possible to compare city plans and enjoy lagoon scenery not present on every Tikal itinerary.

The choice depends on your interest in archaeology and your energy levels. For travelers keen to learn more about ancient Maya cities, optional Yaxhá adds another layer of detail. For those who would rather rest after flying, a stroll through Flores may be more sensible: Tikal is still included the following day.

## How to arrange the optional visit

The [standalone Yaxhá excursion](/guatemala/yaxha/yaxha-optional-visit/) is offered after arrival in Petén. Its terms **do not establish a standard duration, price or package of included services**, so it is important to confirm the departure time from the hotel, return transfer, guiding and admission tickets in advance. Park access and visiting hours should also be checked for the travel dates against the administration's current rules.

Three factors are especially important: the flight's actual arrival time, whether the visit fits within park opening hours, and preserving enough time for a full day at Tikal. Moving Yaxhá to the border-crossing day cannot be assumed to be part of the itinerary without a separate program change.

## Frequently asked questions about optional Yaxhá

### Is Yaxhá included in the price of the Guatemala and Belize tour?

No. On the [12-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-belize-maya-world-12-days/), Yaxhá is offered after arrival in Petén as an extra excursion. Its price and included services must be confirmed before booking.

### Will I have to choose between Yaxhá and Tikal?

Tikal is already included for the following day, so there is no direct choice between the two sites. The decision during free time on the arrival day is between resting or exploring Flores and taking an extra trip to Yaxhá, if time allows.

### Can I visit Yaxhá after a late arrival?

That depends on the actual flight schedule, transfer and park opening hours. The [Yaxhá excursion](/guatemala/yaxha/yaxha-optional-visit/) is arranged individually; confirming it without checking the arrival time would be premature.

### Where can I compare tours with Yaxhá included?

The [tours via Yaxhá catalog](/guatemala/place/yaxha/tour/) lists the main itineraries. It is useful for those who want the archaeological visit scheduled in advance rather than offered as an optional activity during free time.

Our selection includes **{{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}** in which [Yaxhá](/guatemala/place/yaxha/) is part of the main itinerary. This Maya city stands in northern [Guatemala](/guatemala/), in Petén department, amid forest and lagoons. Temples, acropolises, squares and roads connecting quarters of the ancient settlement have survived.

When choosing a tour, compare more than the number of countries and overall duration. Look at **what actually happens on the Yaxhá day**, whether [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/) has already been visited, whether [Topoxté](/guatemala/place/topoxte/) is included as well, and where the group goes after the archaeological site. ## Wonders of Guatemala and Belize: Yaxhá on the way to the border

On the [Wonders of Guatemala and Belize tour](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-belize-wonders/), the opening days explore [Antigua](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/), [Panajachel](/guatemala/place/panajachel/) and [Lake Atitlán](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/). Day 4 includes a flight to Flores and an excursion to Tikal. **Day 5** is devoted to Yaxhá, followed by a border crossing into Belize and accommodation in the Mountain Pine Ridge forest reserve area.

The day's description names the northern acropolis, astronomical complex, squares, temples and ancient roads. The program lets travelers discover the archaeological center before heading into Belize's upland forests. Later the route includes [Caracol](/belize/place/caracol/), caves and the Caribbean coast. This combination is well suited to travelers who want Maya archaeological sites alongside nature and seaside relaxation.

An important detail: Yaxhá falls between two busy days involving road journeys and a border crossing. Assess the complete daily schedule rather than treating the archaeological visit as free time for unlimited additional excursions.

## Guatemala, Honduras and Belize: Yaxhá and island-based Topoxté

The [Guatemala, Honduras and Belize route](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-honduras-belize/) combines the historic regions of Guatemala's highlands, [Copán](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/) in Honduras, [Quiriguá](/guatemala/place/quirigua/) and the river landscapes of [Río Dulce](/guatemala/place/rio-dulce/). The archaeological segment in Petén follows.

**Day 7** visits two sites: Yaxhá and [Topoxté](/guatemala/place/topoxte/). Both are in the same lake region, but Topoxté is on an island and relates to later phases of Maya history. The program includes a return to the hotel after this excursion. **Day 8 is dedicated separately to Tikal.** Travelers can thus compare a mainland city, island ruins and a major ceremonial center without squeezing all three into one short stop.

This option particularly suits archaeology enthusiasts interested in different types of ancient settlements. Pay attention to the water crossing to Topoxté: the possibility of reaching the island does not by itself confirm which transport services are included. Consult the selected product's published terms.

## Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador and Belize: Yaxhá on a four-country itinerary

The [four-country program](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-honduras-el-salvador-belize/) first visits Antigua, Chichicastenango and Atitlán, then [San Salvador](/el-salvador/place/san-salvador/) and [Copán](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/). Travelers next continue towards [Livingston](/guatemala/place/livingston/), [Petén](/guatemala/place/peten/) and Tikal.

**Day 10** is devoted to Yaxhá National Park, followed by a transfer to [San Ignacio](/belize/place/san-ignacio/) in Belize. The description includes a walk through ancient squares and the possibility of seeing a forest panorama near Temple 216. Unlike the tour featuring Topoxté, this program does not identify the island site as a separate obligatory stop.

This tour is best chosen for its broad route through Central America. Yaxhá is an important part of it, but the journey also takes in colonial towns, other archaeological complexes and several national borders.

## How Yaxhá differs from Tikal and Topoxté

Asking "which is better, Yaxhá or Tikal?" misses a key difference. [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/) is known for its huge archaeological complex and high temples rising above the forest. [Yaxhá](/guatemala/place/yaxha/) reveals another Maya city surrounded by lagoons and extensive woodland. Hundreds of structures have been recorded there; notable sites include the northern acropolis, squares and Temple 216 overlooking the lake.

[Topoxté](/guatemala/place/topoxte/) is more different still: an island site especially valuable for studying the Postclassic period. Visiting it requires a boat crossing. An itinerary naming all three sites therefore provides a more varied introduction to Maya archaeology than one limited to a single temple complex.

| Place | Key distinction |
|---|---|
| [Yaxhá](/guatemala/place/yaxha/) | City and lagoons |
| [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/) | Tall temples |
| [Topoxté](/guatemala/place/topoxte/) | Island ruins |
| [Copán](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/) | Carved stelae |
| [Quiriguá](/guatemala/place/quirigua/) | Monumental sculpture |

You can also compare archaeology-focused programs in our [Guatemala cultural and historical tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/guatemala/) section. For travelers interested in Petén's forests and animals, see our [Guatemala nature and wildlife journeys](/interests/wildlife/tours/guatemala/). These catalogs cover different routes; a cultural or nature theme does not itself establish a visit to Yaxhá.

## Planning your visit to Yaxhá

Exploring the archaeological complex involves walking between squares, stairways and ancient roads. Comfortable shoes with good grip are essential. Northern Guatemala is hot and humid, and rain is possible; water, a hat and rain protection are useful even if the itinerary allows only a few hours at the site.

Yaxhá lies within Yaxhá–Nakum–Naranjo National Park. Its habitats are important for birds and other wildlife. You may hear howler monkeys or spot birds along the way, but sightings of quetzals or any rare species are never guaranteed. Wildlife encounters depend on season, weather and luck.

When choosing travel dates, look at the surrounding itinerary. On two routes, Yaxhá precedes the Belize border crossing; on the third, it is visited with island-based Topoxté. Roads, border procedures and the additional boat crossing can affect the day's length. Check park hours, accessible areas, tickets and current border requirements closer to departure, since information from previous seasons may be outdated.

## Frequently asked questions about tours via Yaxhá

### How many Ada Tours itineraries include Yaxhá?

The current figure appears in the catalog above and changes automatically as programs are added or archived. Only tours with Yaxhá on the main route are counted here, not every [Guatemala tour](/guatemala/tour/).

### Are Yaxhá and Tikal visited on the same day?

In the published programs discussed here, they are on **different days**. For example, on Wonders of Guatemala and Belize, Tikal is scheduled for day 4 and Yaxhá for day 5. Check the sequence on the [specific tour page](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-belize-wonders/).

### Does every tour through Yaxhá also visit Topoxté?

No. The separate island site is explicitly listed in the [Guatemala, Honduras and Belize itinerary](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-honduras-belize/). On the other two routes considered, Yaxhá appears without a separate stop at Topoxté.

### Is special physical preparation required?

A normal visit to the accessible squares is a walking excursion through an archaeological park, with uneven paths and stairs. Climbing individual buildings and access to specific areas depend on park rules. Travelers with mobility limitations should check the exact sightseeing route.

### Can I combine Yaxhá with Belize?

Yes. All three described programs link [Guatemala](/guatemala/) with [Belize](/belize/), but differ in the number of other countries and the sequence of archaeological stops. Compare days and transport, not just the route's name.

## Excursions to San Antonio Aguas Calientes: weaving and Maya traditions

[San Antonio Aguas Calientes](/guatemala/place/san-antonio-aguas-calientes/) is a village in Sacatepéquez department, near [Antigua Guatemala](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/). It is known for fabrics with geometric designs, striking color combinations and traditional backstrap weaving. Unlike a souvenir storefront in a larger city, here visitors have an opportunity to see how objects preserving aspects of local culture are made.

Ada Tours offers the [Antigua and the Textile Traditions of San Antonio and Santiago Zamora route](/guatemala/antigua-guatemala/antigua-san-antonio-santiago-zamora-textiles/). It includes a historical walk around Antigua, followed by a visit to San Antonio Aguas Calientes and an encounter with women artisans in Santiago Zamora. It is a separate excursion conducted with an English-speaking guide.

## What makes local weaving interesting

One of the principal traditional tools is the backstrap loom. The weaver secures one end of the warp and controls its tension with her own body. This technique allows intricate patterns to be woven and differs from industrial textile production: the design emerges through a succession of manual operations.

Traditional garments, belts, bags, tablecloths and decorative textiles are among the items made. Craft markets can carry work from different regions of Guatemala, so **the place of sale is not always the place of manufacture**. If you would like to buy a piece made by a local artisan, ask about its maker, technique and materials.

Official publications from Guatemala's tourism institute, INGUAT, describe the local craft market as a place where women weave on backstrap looms and sell textile products. This helps explain the village's specialization, but whether a particular market or workshop is visited depends on the excursion itinerary.

## How the excursion from Antigua unfolds

The [combined Ada Tours excursion](/guatemala/antigua-guatemala/antigua-san-antonio-santiago-zamora-textiles/) begins in Antigua's historic center. The town is known for colonial architecture, old churches, squares and views of the surrounding volcanoes. The journey then continues to settlements where craft traditions are still practiced.

In San Antonio, the main focus is weaving and textile products. The next stop, Santiago Zamora, highlights the traditions of a local group of artisans and the culture of the Kaqchikel Maya. These visits allow travelers to compare two craft settings in a single day.

The program includes **English-language guiding services and admission tickets as specified in the selected itinerary**. Particular workshops, purchases, additional activities and personal expenses are not separately guaranteed. If you would like to try weaving yourself, arrange this in advance.

## San Antonio and Santiago Zamora: what is the difference?

| Stop | Main focus |
|---|---|
| Antigua | History and architecture |
| San Antonio | Weaving |
| Santiago Zamora | Maya women artisans |

San Antonio Aguas Calientes and Santiago Zamora are **different settlements** near Antigua. On the complete route, they complement one another but do not replace the visit to the historic town.

The village should not be confused with San Antonio Palopó on Lake Atitlán. Parts of their names are similar, but the two places are in different areas and belong to different excursion routes.

## Useful information before your visit

Allow time at the workshops to speak with artisans and watch them work. Buying souvenirs remains a personal choice; prices, card payment options and the availability of particular items should be checked locally. Ask permission before photographing people or their work.

The area can experience sudden tropical rain, especially during the wet season. A light jacket and comfortable shoes are useful for walking. If you are primarily interested in learning textile-making techniques in depth, discuss the length of each stop while selecting your [excursion](/guatemala/antigua-guatemala/antigua-san-antonio-santiago-zamora-textiles/).

Other routes focused on local traditions can be found among [Culture and History journeys](/interests/culture-and-history/) and [Guatemala tours](/guatemala/tour/).
